title: Introducing Audited ZDR on AI Gateway
description: AI is now used in every part of a business, and as a result, companies send source code, customer records, and regulated data through inference providers. The assurance that no data is retained after processing is still publicly unverified. Payment platforms, cloud infrastructure, and most other layers that handle data this sensitive have a way to prove their controls to outside parties, and inference will follow the same path. Today we are introducing Audited ZDR on AI Gateway. A provider is labeled Audited ZDR only after an independent security firm tests its zero data retention claims against its code, infrastructure, and live traffic, then publishes the report. Baseten , Modal , and Wafer are launch partners that have already begun audits, and more providers are encouraged to join to help raise the bar for security and privacy. Audited ZDR builds on two steps we took toward stronger governance earlier this year: We launched team-wide Zero Data Retention (ZDR) so teams could route traffic exclusively to providers stating a ZDR policy. We completed our ISO/IEC 42001:2023 certification , which put Vercel’s own AI systems under independent third-party audit. We are now asking inference providers for the same thing we asked of ourselves: independent verification. Why a contract is not enough ZDR guarantees rely on contracts and self-attestation. A provider agrees not to retain prompts or completions, and customers take that commitment on faith. For teams sending proprietary code, customer information, or regulated data through models, self-reported ZDR contracts don't provide enough assurance. Are prompts landing in debug logs, crash dumps, or tracing pipelines? Can a rate limit push a request marked ZDR to a non-ZDR endpoint? Can a support engineer's debugging tools surface a customer's prompt? Answering these questions means running a bespoke security review for every provider and the models they host. An audit answers them in public. What Audited ZDR verifies To qualify for Audited ZDR on AI Gateway, an inference provider engages an independent security firm, chosen from among respected third-party auditors, to run the audit. The firm then tests the provider's zero data retention policy across the serving path for every model, endpoint, feature, and tool that handles AI Gateway traffic. The audit confirms that customer data is never written or retained on durable storage in any system. Customer data means prompts, completions, system prompts, embeddings, files, images and audio, tool and function-call payloads, and any derived data that could identify them. Coverage spans request logs, traces, metrics, crash dumps, prompt caches, abuse monitoring, analytics, backups, support tools, and training, fine-tuning, and evaluation datasets. The audit confirms that once a response is returned to AI Gateway, that content is deleted from the inference provider’s systems. Where a request uses caching, such as a KV cache, the cache stays in RAM only, is never written to disk, and the behavior is disclosed. The audit also confirms: That a request marked ZDR never fails over to a non-ZDR endpoint, tool, or feature That no human or automated process accesses customer data outside handling the request itself That sub-processors with access comply with all of the above That no training on customer data occurs Auditors verify this by reviewing the inference provider's serving-path source code and infrastructure configuration, then running live tests. They send marked prompts through AI Gateway and search the provider's logging, caching, and storage systems for any trace of them. Every passing provider publishes the report under the auditor's name. It covers scope, methodology, dates, findings, and fix status, with any exceptions disclosed and redactions limited to exploit detail. AI Gateway links directly to the report. Canary monitoring between audits An independent audit checks a provider's code and infrastructure at a point in time, but production systems change. To add a detection layer between independent audits, Vercel also runs canary audits against inference providers on AI Gateway. Each run sends prompts containing unique, unindexed URLs mapped privately to a provider, model, and run. Because a ZDR provider should never retain, inspect, or crawl prompt content, any request to a canary URL triggers an investigation into the provider and model involved. Canary checks cannot detect prompts written to disk and never read, so they complement independent code and infrastructure audits rather than replacing them. How Audited ZDR works in AI Gateway We are adding an independently Audited ZDR provider tier and a team-wide toggle in AI Gateway policy settings. When enabled, AI Gateway routes and fails over your team's requests only across providers with published audits that meet the bar. Launch partners have started their audits, and each provider enters the tier as soon as its report is published. Launch partner reports are expected to be published by December 8, 2026. About AI Gateway AI Gateway provides a unified API for calling models, tracking usage and cost, and configuring retries and failover for higher uptime than connecting to providers directly. It reflects provider pricing with no markup and charges no platform fee on inference, including Bring Your Own Key (BYOK) requests. Read the AI Gateway documentation to get started. The audited tier works alongside AI Gateway's other compliance controls. Regional inference pins where a provider runs inference to the US, EU, Australia, or Japan, per request or team-wide, and any data the provider stores at rest stays in that region. If AI Gateway can't honor the region, the request fails rather than running elsewhere. Provider headquarters filters routing by who owns the provider, so a request only reaches providers whose parent company is headquartered in a country you allow. Private inference connects your own self-hosted or fine-tuned model endpoints to AI Gateway, called as private/<slug> with the same SDKs, auth, and observability as catalog models and scoped to your team. Read more

title: AI Gateway now supports extraction models
description: Extraction models are now on AI Gateway. They find specific details in the content you provide, such as an invoice number or contact names, and return them as separate fields your code can use. ScaleDown Extract-1 is the first available extraction model. It extracts text values or lists of text values from text, images, and PDFs. You can use it to process invoices, contracts, and other records. Extraction is currently available through the AI SDK only. With ai@7.0.176 or later, use experimental_extract and the model ID scaledown/extract-1 : Each key in fields has an entry in result.answers . If a field is not found, its value is null . Extract-1 returns confidence scores from 0 to 1 for matches, including individual list items, so you can flag uncertain results for review. For text input, it can also return character offsets showing where a match appears. To extract from a PDF or image, pass it as a file part in state : Extraction requests appear in AI Gateway logs and spend tracking. See the extraction quickstart for setup and authentication. Read more

title: Catch missing feature flags before they reach production
description: Vercel Flags can now block a deployment from reaching production if you’ve declared a flag in code but haven’t created it in your project. Without that definition, your app can silently fall back to the flag’s default value, even if that turns on a feature you meant to keep off. The Flag Definitions Present Deployment Check runs when a deployment is ready. If any flags are missing, the check fails and lists them in the results, where you can create each one before redeploying. The check reads your Flags SDK discovery endpoint. With flags@4.5.0 or later on Vercel, it works without FLAGS_SECRET ; earlier versions still require the secret. To turn on blocking, teams on all plans can enable the check in their project’s Build and Deployment settings and mark it as required. See the Deployment Checks documentation for setup details. Read more

title: Choose AI Gateway providers by headquarters country
description: Provider headquarters sends your AI Gateway requests only to providers headquartered in countries you choose, so you can meet compliance and procurement rules about where your AI vendors are located. You can configure provider headquarters to be an allowlist of the countries to use, or a denylist of the countries to block. AI Gateway skips providers in blocked countries and routes requests to the rest of the list, so a model stays accessible as long as it is available in one of its allowed provider locations. Use provider headquarters with regional hosting and regional inference to control where a request is received, where the model runs, and who runs it. Set provider headquarters for your team Pro and Enterprise customers can apply their provider headquarters list to every AI Gateway request across their team. Configure the list in AI Gateway settings . Provider headquarters settings are applied automatically as AI Gateway adds models and providers. Providers without a headquarters country on record never receive your requests. Set provider headquarters per request On any plan, set headquarters in the gateway provider options to restrict a single request. Pass country codes for an allowlist, or prefix every code with ! for a denylist, as in ['!US'] . If your team has a list, a request can only narrow it. In the examples below, requests are only sent to providers based in the US and Germany: Both settings filter providers, so a model stays available as long as one of its providers is based in an allowed country. If no provider is available in an allowed country, AI Gateway tries your fallback models. If no fallback models are available in allowed countries, or if no fallback models are configured, the request will fail without trying to route to providers in other locations. Read the provider headquarters documentation for the countries supported, pricing and setup details. Read more

title: MAI-Image-2.7 and MAI-Image-2.7-Flash now available on AI Gateway
description: Microsoft’s MAI-Image-2.7 and MAI-Image-2.7-Flash are now available in public preview on AI Gateway . Both increase the maximum output size to 2048 x 2048 pixels and add transparent backgrounds for generated and edited images. Generate images from text or edit existing images with one AI Gateway API key, without a Microsoft account. Both models support photorealistic images, text rendering, and targeted edits to products, portraits, and layouts. Use up to five reference images to guide edits or combine subjects. MAI-Image-2.7 ( microsoft/mai-image-2.7 ): for final assets where image quality is the priority MAI-Image-2.7-Flash ( microsoft/mai-image-2.7-flash ): for faster, lower-cost generation when exploring prompts or creating variations Set the AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY environment variable, then use either model ID with AI SDK 6 or later . To generate a transparent PNG, set providerOptions.azure.background to 'transparent' : To edit an image, provide it as a reference and describe what to change: You can also generate and edit images from the terminal with the AI CLI , using the same API key and model IDs: Try MAI-Image-2.7 or MAI-Image-2.7-Flash in the model playground, or follow the image generation guide . Read more

title: GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol now available on AI Gateway
description: GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol from OpenAI are now available on AI Gateway . GPT-6.2 Astra: for complex, multi-step projects, with improvements to implementing and testing changes in existing codebases, following document templates, and computer use GPT-6.2 Sol: for everyday coding, writing, and agent workflows, including building interactive web applications from a written brief Use openai/gpt-6.2-astra or openai/gpt-6.2-sol as the model ID. For the API examples, set AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY to your AI Gateway API key . Both models also support the Responses API . For lower latency at higher per-token rates, both models support fast mode and OpenAI’s Ultrafast service tier . To request Ultrafast, set providerOptions.openai.serviceTier to 'ultrafast' in the AI SDK, or set service_tier to 'ultrafast' in Chat Completions and Responses requests. GPT-6.2 Astra’s Ultrafast output-token price is 60% lower than GPT-6 Astra’s. To use the models in coding agents like Codex, Cursor, and more, install the latest Vercel CLI and run setup: Then select openai/gpt-6.2-astra or openai/gpt-6.2-sol in the agent. See the coding agents guide for details. Try GPT-6.2 Astra or GPT-6.2 Sol in the playground, or compare OpenAI models . Read more
